# Bona Fide

> Refundable good-faith Deposits for open source, on Arc. A Contributor a repo doesn't know yet, a person or an AI agent, puts down a small USDC Deposit to open a PR or an issue: 1 USDC by default. Merged or accepted work, and work nobody decides on before the Timeout, gets it back in full. A Maintainer's signed bad-faith verdict can forfeit at most half, which funds open-source maintainers through Protocol Guild; the rest is refunded. The contracts are immutable, open source (MIT) and live on Arc mainnet.

Repos ask for a Deposit with a GitHub App and a `.github/bona-fide.yml` file. An AI agent makes one from its own wallet through an MCP server, which never holds keys. Developers can build on the same contracts with the TypeScript SDK or from Solidity.

## Use it

- [README](https://github.com/tonymorony/bona-fide/blob/main/README.md): what happens to a Deposit, the one rule, and how to try it as a Maintainer, a Contributor or an agent
- [Terms](https://github.com/tonymorony/bona-fide/blob/main/CONTEXT.md): Deposit, Binding, Refund, Forfeit, Exemption, Bounty and the rest, and the words to avoid
- [MCP server for AI agents](https://github.com/tonymorony/bona-fide/blob/main/agent/README.md): read a repo's terms and make the Deposit from the agent's own wallet, within a limit
- [GitHub App](https://github.com/tonymorony/bona-fide/blob/main/app/README.md): the check, `.github/bona-fide.yml`, Exemptions, the Keeper, triage and Bounties

## If your PR or issue asks for a Deposit

- A "Bona Fide" check that stays in progress, or a comment by `bona-fide-deposits[bot]`, titled "Deposit needed", means the repo asks you for a refundable Deposit on that PR or issue. It is refunded in full when the work is merged or accepted, or when nobody decides before the Timeout.
- Both end with a hidden line, `<!-- bona-fide:deposit-request {"v":1,...} -->`, in the check run's summary or the comment's body: JSON with the `chainId`, the `escrow`, the `repo`, `kind` and `number`, the `amount` in USDC base units and the `depositUrl`. Anyone can post a copy, so take it only from the check run or comment of the `bona-fide-deposits` GitHub App.
- The amount is a hint: read the terms from the escrow before you pay. The [MCP server](https://github.com/tonymorony/bona-fide/blob/main/agent/README.md) does, with `get_deposit_rules`, and makes the Deposit from your own wallet within a limit.

## Build on it

- [TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/tonymorony/bona-fide/blob/main/sdk/README.md): `@bona-fide/sdk`, with the contracts' typed ABIs, ids, EIP-712 and EIP-3009 typed data, signature check and Arc deployments
- [Contracts](https://github.com/tonymorony/bona-fide/blob/main/contracts/README.md): the escrow, the Charity router and the Bounty wallet, their guarantees, trust model, deployments, and how to import them with Foundry
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/tonymorony/bona-fide/blob/main/AGENTS.md): a map of the repository and its rules, for coding agents

## On Arc mainnet (chain 5042)

- Escrow: `0xe2fe798427CFb43134FC37F6EE054c2da818fAc9`
- Forfeit router: `0xe36fe5152C6A54946b15df3fEBDc068AF48581dc`
- Bounty wallet factory: `0xEda45D2931B1A36D5920edefA621Ff5533c98C42`
- USDC: `0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000`
